reason.description: Why the lease is needed, which a lease that needs approval asks for.

item.description: The item's number in the workspace's repository, or its URL.

AgentStatus.description: A workspace's agent and its state.

agent.description: The agent's name, such as `claude`, when known.

since.description: Unix seconds since the state was reported, when known.

AgentToQueue.description: An agent to queue in a workspace once it is ready.

agent.description: The agent to start, such as `claude` or `codex`.

prompt.description: The agent's first message; without one it waits for the user.

shown.description:
The question as shown. When given, a question that no longer matches
it, such as a later one reusing its number, is refused with `not_found`.

approval.description: The approval request of an `approval_pending` or `approval_denied` refusal.

Approval.description: A workspace's request for the user's approval.

id.description: The number it is decided by; reused once the request is gone.

key.description: What names this request for good, unlike its number.

proposal.description: The issue or PR a proposal opens once approved.

subject.description:
What the user is asked to decide, such as `simulator (lease)` or
`open issue "Flaky test"`.

target.description: What it authorizes, such as `simulator`, `port/web` or `pr_open`.

Check.description: One CI check of a PR.

state.description: The forge's state, such as `success`, `failure` or `pending`.

cleanup.description: Whether the workspace is removed once it qualifies.

base.description: What the branch starts from; the default branch when absent.

issue.description: The issue the workspace is assigned, by number or URL.

name.description: The new branch; the workspace takes the name derived from it.

pr.description: The PR the workspace works on, by number or URL, linked once it is ready.

repository.description: The repository's ID, name or path.

shown.description:
The request as shown. When given, a request that no longer matches
it, such as a later one reusing its number, is refused with `not_found`.

Event.description:
What a subscription sends: its snapshot in one or more parts, then each
change. After a daemon restart the connection closes; a new subscription
starts with a new snapshot.

oneOf.description:
Some of the records the subscription covers, as they are now;
`complete` marks the last part.
A record was added or changed, and is now `record`.
The record `key` names was removed.
An event this version does not know; ignore it.

after.description:
Skip the events before this index, as when following again after
reading them.

oneOf.description: The daemon refused the connection, such as with `unsupported_version`.

client.description: The client's name, for the daemon's log.

scope.description: A workspace's scope token; without one the caller is the user.

version.description: The API version the client speaks, such as `1.0.0`.

Hold.description: A named claim that a workspace is still in use.

push.description: Push the default branch after landing; `[land] push` when absent.

fast_forward.description: Whether the default branch fast-forwarded rather than taking a merge commit.

previous_commit.description: The default branch's commit before landing.

pushed_to.description: The remote the default branch was pushed to.

updated.description: False when the default branch already contained the branch.

Link.description:
An issue or PR a workspace links, with its state as the daemon last
recorded it from the forge.

checks.description: A PR's CI checks on its head.

conflict.description:
Whether a PR's head conflicts with its base; absent when unknown,
such as while the forge has not checked a new head or base.

head.description: A PR's head commit, which its checks ran on.

lookup_errors.description:
What the daemon could not read when it last looked, such as CI
checks; what it covers may be older than the rest.

state.description:
The forge's state, such as `open`, `closed` or `merged`; absent until
the daemon has looked.

LookupError.description: A part of an item the daemon could not read from its forge.

source.description: What it could not read, such as `CI`.

cleanup.description: Remove the workspace once it qualifies, even where `[cleanup.done] enabled` is false.

Message.description: A message to a workspace's agent or from one to the user.

attachments.description: Shoal's copies of the attached files.

text.description: Empty when the message is only its attachments.

workspace_id.description: The workspace's ID, for a message to its agent.

Notification.description: Something the daemon tells the user.

workspace.description: The workspace's name when it happened.

base.description: The branch it merges into; the default branch when absent.

body.description:
The description as written; `Closes #<issue>` when absent and an
issue is linked.

draft.description: Open it as a draft, or not; the repository's default when absent.

title.description: The linked issue's title when absent.

created.description: Whether this call opened it, rather than finding it open.

linked.description: Whether the workspace links it now.

warnings.description: What the PR lacks of the repository's conventions.

Opening.description:
The client's first frame. Its `client_api` key tells the daemon the
connection speaks this API rather than Shoal's internal protocol.

OperationEvent.description: The `index`th event of an operation, from 0.

oneOf.description: A line its processes wrote, without its line ending.
Progress this version does not know; ignore it.
The created or split workspace, ready, and the agent queued in it.
The workspace's PR, opened or found open.

The PR waits for the user's approval before Shoal opens it, as the
repository's `[permissions] pr_open` asks of workspace agents.
A result this version does not know.

ProposedItem.description: The issue or PR a proposal opens.

Question.description: An open question a workspace's agent asked the user.

id.description: The number it is answered by; reused once the question is gone.

agent.description: The agent to start, such as `claude` or `codex`.

prompt.description: The agent's first message; without one it waits for the user.

position.description: Its place among waiting entries, from 1; absent once starting.

ReadyMark.description: A statement that linked work is ready for review at a commit.

item.description: The marked issue or PR; absent when the mark covers the workspace.

Record.description: One record, tagged with its kind as `type`.

oneOf.description: A kind this version does not know; ignore it.

RecordKey.description:
What names a record among those of its kind. The ID is opaque: compare
it, never parse it.

branch_deleted.description: Whether the branch was deleted; it is kept when only it has some commits.

hook_error.description: Why the best-effort removal hook failed, after a removal that succeeded.

item.description: The item's number in the workspace's repository, or its URL.

discard_unsaved.description:
Delete uncommitted files and the commits of a detached HEAD. Without
it, a workspace with either is refused with `unsaved_work`.

branch.description: The new branch name; the workspace takes the name derived from it.

name.description: The name it was registered under, if any.

source.description: The path or URL it was registered from.

Request.description: A request; its responses carry its ID.

oneOf.description: Every registered repository, most recently used first.

Fetch a repository's default branch from its remote and
fast-forward the local default branch.
Remove a workspace as `shoal rm` does, keeping a checkpoint.
Record the workspace's assignment as done, as `shoal done` does.
Withdraw a recorded completion, as `shoal done --undo` does.
Rename the workspace's branch, and the workspace with it.

Queue an agent in the workspace, which the daemon starts detached
in the default host once the agent queue admits it.
Stop what runs in the workspace, saving its agent's session.

Approve or deny a request: the user any, a workspace's agent only
those its children's agents passed to it, as with `shoal approvals`.

Create a workspace and start its setup, as `shoal add` does; the
operation ends with the ready workspace.

Split a child from the workspace and start its setup, as
`shoal split` does.

Push the workspace's branch, then open its PR or link the open
one, as `shoal pr open` does.

Land the workspace's branch on the default branch, as `shoal
land` does; a workspace agent's landing waits for approval.

Interrupt an operation's running step, as an interrupt of the
command that runs it does.

The records of the topics asked for: a snapshot, then their
changes, until the client hangs up.

An operation's progress, from the start or after the events
already read, then its result or error. An operation can be
followed until ten minutes after it ended.

Response.description:
One response to a request. A result too large for one frame arrives as
`page` frames holding the first items of its list, then a `result`
holding the rest.

oneOf.description: A subscription's records, until the client hangs up.
An operation's progress, until its `result` or `error`.

SimulatorLease.description: A simulator leased to a workspace.

base.description: What the branch starts from; the default branch when absent.

issue.description: The issue the child is assigned, by number or URL.

name.description: The child's new branch; the child takes the name derived from it.

workspace.description: The workspace to split the new one from.
The workspace it works in, as it is when it starts.

topics.description: A daemon skips topics it does not know.

repository.description: The repository's ID, name or path.

remote.description: The default branch's upstream remote, absent when it has none.

features.description:
The methods and subscription topics the daemon offers, such as
`workspace.get` and `topic:workspaces`.

supported_majors.description: The major versions the daemon serves.

version.description: The API version the daemon speaks.

Workspace.description: A workspace: a worktree on its own branch, with what Shoal records about it.

agent.description: Its agent, when one runs, waits in the queue or stopped with a session to restore.

base_workspace.description: The workspace whose branch this one builds on.

done.description: Its assignment is done and the completion not withdrawn.

error.description: Why the workspace failed or needs repair.

holds.description: Holds that keep it from cleanup.

parent_workspace.description: The workspace this one was split from.

ready_marks.description: Marks that its work is ready for review.

title.description: What its agent calls the work.

WorkspaceRef.description: Another workspace a record refers to.
